us.title: China moves to prop up stocks with selling curbs, buybacks after 10% slide this year
us.description: State buying and selling curbs typically put a floor under Chinese equities in the short term, so near-term downside in mainland indices may be more limited than global tech peers suggest. That support is administrative rather than fundamental, and rallies built on directed buying have often faded once the intervention eases. The yuan and Chinese government bonds, which have held up well this year, are unlikely to be driven by the measures. Monday’s GDP and activity data matter more: a weak print could raise hopes of fiscal stimulus, which would give equities firmer footing than market support alone. Broader Asian tech sentiment will hinge on global AI valuations. China Q3 GDP beats estimates, as does September retail sales Beijing is reaching for its familiar toolkit of state buying and polite instructions not to sell, but propping up share prices is easier than fixing the weak demand dragging on the economy. Summary: Chinese regulators asked companies and state-backed funds to buy shares and guided some investors to sell less, Bloomberg reported Major insurers were told to report equity holdings, avoid crystallising losses below cost and align investments with economic goals The “national team” of state funds was asked to speed up purchases, with signs of heavy ETF inflows The benchmark index is down about 10% this year and hit its lowest since August 2025, amid a global sell-off in AI-linked tech Chinese bonds and the yuan have held up, with the yuan up more than 4% against the dollar this year The measures come ahead of Q3 GDP, expected to show growth below Beijing’s target Chinese authorities have stepped in to support the country’s stock market, asking state funds and companies to buy shares while discouraging some investors from selling, according to a Bloomberg report, as a tech-led slide pushed the benchmark index down about 10% this year. Financial regulators held a meeting on Thursday at which they asked companies and state-backed funds to purchase stocks and guided some investors to reduce selling, Bloomberg reported, citing people familiar with the matter. State funds, often referred to as the “national team”, were asked to accelerate their buying, and separate reporting pointed to heavy inflows into exchange-traded funds consistent with state purchases. Major insurers received informal window guidance to report their equity holdings, avoid locking in losses on positions trading below cost, and align their investment decisions with broader economic objectives. Regulators did not respond to requests for comment. The steps build on commitments from the securities regulator earlier this month to strengthen market-stabilisation mechanisms, widen channels for long-term institutional money, encourage higher dividends and share buybacks, and prepare further policy tools. The intervention follows a sharp sell-off concentrated in technology and AI-related shares, which had led earlier gains. The benchmark index closed on Thursday at its lowest since August 2025, while the tech-heavy ChiNext index fell almost 3% that day. The weakness was part of a wider global retreat from AI-linked stocks, with South Korea’s Kospi falling more than 7% and Japan’s Nikkei 225 almost 5% on the same day as investors reassessed valuations and interest-rate expectations. According to Bloomberg, authorities are concerned about market fragility and want to prevent selling pressure from feeding a downward spiral. Notably, the stress has been concentrated in equities rather than spreading across Chinese assets. Government bonds have rallied this year, pushing the 10-year yield close to its lowest in more than a year, while the yuan has gained more than 4% against the dollar, outperforming its Asian peers. The support measures come as the economy struggles with weak consumer demand, sluggish private investment and a prolonged property downturn. Monday’s third-quarter GDP data is expected to show growth below Beijing’s 4.5% to 5.0% target. That sets up a broader test. Administrative steps such as selling curbs and directed buying can steady prices in the short term, but they do little to address the weak domestic demand behind the economic slowdown. Whether Beijing follows up with more substantial fiscal or monetary support may matter more for a durable recovery in Chinese stocks. This article was written by Eamonn Sheridan at investinglive.com.

sg.title: ESMO 2026 Preview | Mabwell to Present Clinical Results for Nectin-4-Targeting ADC 9MW2821 in ADC-Pretreated Triple-Negative Breast Cancer
sg.description: SHANGHAI, Oct. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Mabwell (688062.SH, 02493.HK), an innovation-driven biopharmaceutical company with a fully integrated industry chain, will present Phase II clinical data on its Nectin-4-targeting antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) 9MW2821 (Bulumtatug Fuvedotin, "BFv") in locally advanced or metastatic triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) as an oral presentation at the 2026 European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) Congress. The study focuses on patients previously treated with an ADC carrying a topoisomerase I inhibitor payload (hereinafter "Topo I ADC-pretreated"). The abstract is now available on the congress website. The study (CTR20242376) is designed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of 9MW2821 as monotherapy or in combination with a PD-1 monoclonal antibody in patients with locally advanced or metastatic TNBC. As of April 10, 2026, among 60 efficacy-evaluable Topo I ADC-pretreated patients, the objective response rate (ORR) was 30.0%, the disease control rate (DCR) was 80.0%, the median progression-free survival (mPFS) was 3.7 months, the median duration of response (mDOR) was 8.7 months, and the median overall survival (mOS) was not yet mature. No new safety signals were observed during this follow-up period. The study results indicate that 9MW2821 has a manageable safety profile and positive therapeutic effects in patients with TNBC. In 2024, an estimated 375,800 women in China were newly diagnosed with breast cancer and approximately 73,000 died of the disease[1]. TNBC accounts for approximately 15%–20% of all breast cancers and is highly aggressive with a poor prognosis. Currently, all ADCs approved for TNBC use a topoisomerase I inhibitor payload. After progression on these agents, chemotherapy remains the mainstay of care and new treatment options are urgently needed. [1] Xia C, Li H, Wu C, Chen W. Cancer burden and control in China. Nat Rev Clin Oncol. 2026. doi:10.1038/s41571-026-01165-8 About 9MW2821 9MW2821 is a Nectin-4-targeting ADC independently developed by Mabwell on its proprietary ADC development platform. It is currently conducting multiple clinical studies for several indications including urothelial carcinoma (UC), cervical cancer (CC), triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC), and esophageal cancer (EC), with a cumulative clinical enrollment of over 2,200 patients. Currently, four pivotal Phase III clinical trials of 9MW2821 are underway, including UC monotherapy and combination therapy, CC monotherapy, and monotherapy for topoisomerase I inhibitor-payload ADC-pretreated TNBC. 9MW2821 has been granted Breakthrough Therapy Designation by the Center for Drug Evaluation (CDE) for UC, both as monotherapy and in combination therapy. It is the first Nectin-4-targeting agent to enter Phase III clinical study in CC, and the first agent of any target to enter Phase III clinical study specifically in patients with Topo I ADC-pretreated TNBC. The Phase III clinical trials of 9MW2821 for UC monotherapy, UC combination therapy, and CC monotherapy are planned to undergo interim analyses in 2026, and it is expected to, based on the interim analysis data, submit applications for pre-NDA meetings to the CDE under the National Medical Products Administration (NMPA). Multiple Phase I/II clinical trials are ongoing in parallel and progressing rapidly. In addition, the TNBC (Topo I ADC-pretreated) monotherapy has entered into Phase Ib clinical trials in the United States. About Mabwell Mabwell (688062.SH, 02493.HK) is an innovation-driven biopharmaceutical company with capabilities spanning the entire pharmaceutical value chain. sg.title: Edvance and CWG Launch RealRelay Fintech, AI Agents for Finance with Trust Built First
sg.description: Edvance and CWG open RealRelay's third vertical, bringing tested and rated AI agents to finance as MAS sets out how AI in the sector should be governed. SINGAPORE, Oct. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- On Oct. 17, Edvance International Holdings Limited (HKEX: 1410) ("Edvance"), through its wholly-owned Singapore subsidiary Paradise Matrix Pte. Ltd., and CWG Innovations Pte. Ltd. ("CWG") today launched RealRelay Fintech, the third vertical on RealRelay.ai, the platform on which organisations build, test and run AI agents without writing code. The launch took place at a one-day youth AI event at Suntec Convention Centre, co-organised by the Digital Defence Alliance Singapore (DDAS) and CWG with the support of the National Youth Council (NYC). The event was conceptualised, planned and developed by Mr Aaron Ang (linkedin.com/in/aaronangsg), Chief Commercial Officer of CWG, who leads the RealRelay project. Mr Ang built the day around one challenge. Participants were handed a simulated fraud case and asked to use agentic AI to find out what had happened. Within hours they had worked through tens of thousands of transaction records, traced the money, flagged the entries that did not add up and shown how they got there. The same job, done by hand, would take an audit team weeks. The event was graced by Mr Ong Kah Kuang, Assistant Chief Executive of the National Youth Council. That is what RealRelay Fintech sets out to do. Work that is slow, manual and easy to get wrong, such as reconciling accounts, checking documents and finding the one record in a million that should not be there, becomes something an agent on the platform does accurately, in hours, with every step on record. Fraud detection is the clearest example, and it is where the fintech vertical begins. In finance, though, a fast answer counts for nothing unless the institution can trust it. Trust comes first Finance is the sector where trust in AI matters most, and Singapore has moved first. On 7 October the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) issued its Guidelines on AI Risk Management. They cover every financial institution and every form of AI, agents included. Boards are expected to oversee AI risk, keep an inventory of each AI use, manage third-party AI and control the whole life cycle, from testing to monitoring. The guidelines take effect in October 2027. In August, MAS also committed S$220 million under FSTI 4.0 to get AI into the sector faster, including an AI Pathfinder track for solutions listed on PathFin.ai. Every agent on RealRelay passes through the Trust and Control Layer. The platform's own security agent tests it before it goes live and tests it again each time it changes. Permissions, logging, retention and access are controlled centrally, and every agent carries a risk rating that covers the data it can touch, the actions it can take and how it behaved under test. That rating, the agent inventory and the full log are the same things MAS now asks financial institutions to keep. The Trust and Control Layer draws on Edvance's more than 20 years in cybersecurity. Asked what the launch represents, Mr Ang said: "Singapore has been clear about how it wants AI to enter finance. Innovate, but with trust and control in place from the start. We believe that is the next phase of fintech, and we built RealRelay Fintech on exactly that principle. The Trust and Control Layer is the foundation of the platform. Every agent is tested before it goes live, and the institution keeps full control over what it can see and do. When people can see that, they stop hesitating. That is how banks, funds and founders will actually put AI to work, and that is what we are here to make possible." What RealRelay Fintech does At launch the vertical covers four areas of work. Research and analysis. Agents that read filings, news and market data, run scenarios and produce forecasts with the reasoning shown. Decision documents. Credit memos, investment committee packs, portfolio risk briefs and client review notes, drafted from a firm's own data and templates. Fraud, compliance and document checks. Agents that reconcile transactions, flag anomalies, check onboarding documents against policy and keep a record of every check. Learning. A guided track for students and new joiners, using the same tools professionals use, at a price a student can afford. Institutional deployments, including Singapore-hosted and on-premises options, are available on request. Three verticals, one platform RealRelay has two layers sitting on a Trust and Control Layer. The Token Exchange launched on 30 September 2026 and puts more than 300 mainstream AI models behind one subscription, routing each task to a suitable model at a lower cost than buying them separately. The Agentic Layer sits on top. Users describe what they need in plain language, assemble an agent from ready-made modules, test it and deploy it in one click, with no code. Three verticals run on these layers: education, cybersecurity and now fintech. Education came first, and it is where the platform found its first users. At the APEX Bootcamp in September, students and young working adults with no technical background built working agents in two days. Interest from educational institutions has followed, and CWG is finalising details with these institutions to provide RealRelay and the full AI ecosystem around it to their students. Fintech now follows the same path, on the same layers and under the same controls. What comes next RealRelay Fintech will run a series of masterclasses in parallel with the Singapore FinTech Festival from 18 to 20 November 2026, and CWG is preparing its listing on PathFin.ai. Over 2027, the Trust and Control Layer will be mapped to the MAS guidelines so that an institution can take an agent's test record straight into its own risk assessment. Agents built to individual institutions' own policies and templates will follow. For Edvance, fintech opens a subscription market where the buyers are large, regulated, and now required to show trust and control over the AI they use. Edvance is responsible for commercialising the platform and holds the intellectual property in its cybersecurity agents. The platform is owned and operated from Singapore, and the two companies are preparing to take it global, with partner talks under way and expansion plans already in place. ESMO 2026 Preview | Mabwell to Present Clinical Results for Nectin-4-Targeting ADC 9MW2821 in ADC-Pretreated Triple-Negative Breast Cancer
ph.description: SHANGHAI, Oct. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Mabwell (688062.SH, 02493.HK), an innovation-driven biopharmaceutical company with a fully integrated industry chain, will present Phase II clinical data on its Nectin-4-targeting antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) 9MW2821 (Bulumtatug Fuvedotin, "BFv") in locally advanced or metastatic triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) as an oral presentation at the 2026 European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) Congress. The study focuses on patients previously treated with an ADC carrying a topoisomerase I inhibitor payload (hereinafter "Topo I ADC-pretreated"). The abstract is now available on the congress website. The study (CTR20242376) is designed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of 9MW2821 as monotherapy or in combination with a PD-1 monoclonal antibody in patients with locally advanced or metastatic TNBC. As of April 10, 2026, among 60 efficacy-evaluable Topo I ADC-pretreated patients, the objective response rate (ORR) was 30.0%, the disease control rate (DCR) was 80.0%, the median progression-free survival (mPFS) was 3.7 months, the median duration of response (mDOR) was 8.7 months, and the median overall survival (mOS) was not yet mature. No new safety signals were observed during this follow-up period. The study results indicate that 9MW2821 has a manageable safety profile and positive therapeutic effects in patients with TNBC. In 2024, an estimated 375,800 women in China were newly diagnosed with breast cancer and approximately 73,000 died of the disease[1]. TNBC accounts for approximately 15%–20% of all breast cancers and is highly aggressive with a poor prognosis. Currently, all ADCs approved for TNBC use a topoisomerase I inhibitor payload. After progression on these agents, chemotherapy remains the mainstay of care and new treatment options are urgently needed. [1] Xia C, Li H, Wu C, Chen W. Cancer burden and control in China. Nat Rev Clin Oncol. 2026. doi:10.1038/s41571-026-01165-8 About 9MW2821 9MW2821 is a Nectin-4-targeting ADC independently developed by Mabwell on its proprietary ADC development platform. It is currently conducting multiple clinical studies for several indications including urothelial carcinoma (UC), cervical cancer (CC), triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC), and esophageal cancer (EC), with a cumulative clinical enrollment of over 2,200 patients. Currently, four pivotal Phase III clinical trials of 9MW2821 are underway, including UC monotherapy and combination therapy, CC monotherapy, and monotherapy for topoisomerase I inhibitor-payload ADC-pretreated TNBC. 9MW2821 has been granted Breakthrough Therapy Designation by the Center for Drug Evaluation (CDE) for UC, both as monotherapy and in combination therapy. It is the first Nectin-4-targeting agent to enter Phase III clinical study in CC, and the first agent of any target to enter Phase III clinical study specifically in patients with Topo I ADC-pretreated TNBC. The Phase III clinical trials of 9MW2821 for UC monotherapy, UC combination therapy, and CC monotherapy are planned to undergo interim analyses in 2026, and it is expected to, based on the interim analysis data, submit applications for pre-NDA meetings to the CDE under the National Medical Products Administration (NMPA). Multiple Phase I/II clinical trials are ongoing in parallel and progressing rapidly. In addition, the TNBC (Topo I ADC-pretreated) monotherapy has entered into Phase Ib clinical trials in the United States. ph.title: Edvance and CWG Launch RealRelay Fintech, AI Agents for Finance with Trust Built First
ph.description: Edvance and CWG open RealRelay's third vertical, bringing tested and rated AI agents to finance as MAS sets out how AI in the sector should be governed. SINGAPORE, Oct. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- On Oct. 17, Edvance International Holdings Limited (HKEX: 1410) ("Edvance"), through its wholly-owned Singapore subsidiary Paradise Matrix Pte. Ltd., and CWG Innovations Pte. Ltd. ("CWG") today launched RealRelay Fintech, the third vertical on RealRelay.ai, the platform on which organisations build, test and run AI agents without writing code. The launch took place at a one-day youth AI event at Suntec Convention Centre, co-organised by the Digital Defence Alliance Singapore (DDAS) and CWG with the support of the National Youth Council (NYC). The event was conceptualised, planned and developed by Mr Aaron Ang (linkedin.com/in/aaronangsg), Chief Commercial Officer of CWG, who leads the RealRelay project. Mr Ang built the day around one challenge. Participants were handed a simulated fraud case and asked to use agentic AI to find out what had happened. Within hours they had worked through tens of thousands of transaction records, traced the money, flagged the entries that did not add up and shown how they got there. The same job, done by hand, would take an audit team weeks. The event was graced by Mr Ong Kah Kuang, Assistant Chief Executive of the National Youth Council. That is what RealRelay Fintech sets out to do. Work that is slow, manual and easy to get wrong, such as reconciling accounts, checking documents and finding the one record in a million that should not be there, becomes something an agent on the platform does accurately, in hours, with every step on record. Fraud detection is the clearest example, and it is where the fintech vertical begins. In finance, though, a fast answer counts for nothing unless the institution can trust it. Trust comes first Finance is the sector where trust in AI matters most, and Singapore has moved first. On 7 October the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) issued its Guidelines on AI Risk Management. They cover every financial institution and every form of AI, agents included. Boards are expected to oversee AI risk, keep an inventory of each AI use, manage third-party AI and control the whole life cycle, from testing to monitoring. The guidelines take effect in October 2027. In August, MAS also committed S$220 million under FSTI 4.0 to get AI into the sector faster, including an AI Pathfinder track for solutions listed on PathFin.ai. Every agent on RealRelay passes through the Trust and Control Layer. The platform's own security agent tests it before it goes live and tests it again each time it changes. Permissions, logging, retention and access are controlled centrally, and every agent carries a risk rating that covers the data it can touch, the actions it can take and how it behaved under test. That rating, the agent inventory and the full log are the same things MAS now asks financial institutions to keep. The Trust and Control Layer draws on Edvance's more than 20 years in cybersecurity. Asked what the launch represents, Mr Ang said: "Singapore has been clear about how it wants AI to enter finance. Innovate, but with trust and control in place from the start. We believe that is the next phase of fintech, and we built RealRelay Fintech on exactly that principle. The Trust and Control Layer is the foundation of the platform. Every agent is tested before it goes live, and the institution keeps full control over what it can see and do. When people can see that, they stop hesitating. That is how banks, funds and founders will actually put AI to work, and that is what we are here to make possible." What RealRelay Fintech does At launch the vertical covers four areas of work. Research and analysis. Agents that read filings, news and market data, run scenarios and produce forecasts with the reasoning shown. Decision documents. Credit memos, investment committee packs, portfolio risk briefs and client review notes, drafted from a firm's own data and templates. Fraud, compliance and document checks. Agents that reconcile transactions, flag anomalies, check onboarding documents against policy and keep a record of every check. Learning. A guided track for students and new joiners, using the same tools professionals use, at a price a student can afford. Institutional deployments, including Singapore-hosted and on-premises options, are available on request. Three verticals, one platform RealRelay has two layers sitting on a Trust and Control Layer. The Token Exchange launched on 30 September 2026 and puts more than 300 mainstream AI models behind one subscription, routing each task to a suitable model at a lower cost than buying them separately. The Agentic Layer sits on top. Users describe what they need in plain language, assemble an agent from ready-made modules, test it and deploy it in one click, with no code. Three verticals run on these layers: education, cybersecurity and now fintech. Education came first, and it is where the platform found its first users. At the APEX Bootcamp in September, students and young working adults with no technical background built working agents in two days. Interest from educational institutions has followed, and CWG is finalising details with these institutions to provide RealRelay and the full AI ecosystem around it to their students. Fintech now follows the same path, on the same layers and under the same controls. What comes next RealRelay Fintech will run a series of masterclasses in parallel with the Singapore FinTech Festival from 18 to 20 November 2026, and CWG is preparing its listing on PathFin.ai. Over 2027, the Trust and Control Layer will be mapped to the MAS guidelines so that an institution can take an agent's test record straight into its own risk assessment. Agents built to individual institutions' own policies and templates will follow. For Edvance, fintech opens a subscription market where the buyers are large, regulated, and now required to show trust and control over the AI they use. Edvance is responsible for commercialising the platform and holds the intellectual property in its cybersecurity agents. The platform is owned and operated from Singapore, and the two companies are preparing to take it global, with partner talks under way and expansion plans already in place. Paradise Matrix Pte. Ltd. is Edvance's wholly-owned subsidiary in Singapore. For more information, visit https://www.paradisematrix.sg. About CWG Innovations Pte. Ltd. CWG Innovations Pte. Between January and June 2026, IOM’s Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM) monitored cross-border mobility at the Ressano Garcia and Zobue Flow Monitoring Points (FMPs) to better understand movement patterns, migration routes, intended destinations and factors infuencing mobility across Mozambique’s borders. During the reporting period, Flow Monitoring Counting (FMC) recorded 86,814 movements, with entries into and departures from Mozambique each accounting for 50 per cent of observed movements. In parallel, Flow Monitoring Surveys (FMS) were conducted with 5,893 travellers to provide more detailed information on migrant profiles, routes, reasons for movement, intended destinations and potential vulnerabilities. Unless otherwise specified, the analysis presented throughout this report is based on FMS data from the interviewed travellers. Among interviewed travellers who provided information on their intended destination, 36 per cent reported Malawi, followed by South Africa (28%). Cross-border mobility was largely associated with the Mozambique-Malawi and Mozambique-South Africa corridors, including movements linked to trade and employment opportunities. In addition, a separate analysis covering April to July 2026 examines migrants returning from South Africa amid reported protests and related protection concerns, including those transiting through Mozambique towards Malawi.

pk.description: SHANGHAI, Oct. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Mabwell (688062.SH, 02493.HK), an innovation-driven biopharmaceutical company with a fully integrated industry chain, will present Phase II clinical data on its Nectin-4-targeting antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) 9MW2821 (Bulumtatug Fuvedotin, "BFv") in locally advanced or metastatic triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) as an oral presentation at the 2026 European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) Congress. As of April 10, 2026, among 60 efficacy-evaluable Topo I ADC-pretreated patients, the objective response rate (ORR) was 30.0%, the disease control rate (DCR) was 80.0%, the median progression-free survival (mPFS) was 3.7 months, the median duration of response (mDOR) was 8.7 months, and the median overall survival (mOS) was not yet mature. No new safety signals were observed during this follow-up period. The study results indicate that 9MW2821 has a manageable safety profile and positive therapeutic effects in patients with TNBC. In 2024, an estimated 375,800 women in China were newly diagnosed with breast cancer and approximately 73,000 died of the disease[1]. TNBC accounts for approximately 15%–20% of all breast cancers and is highly aggressive with a poor prognosis. Currently, all ADCs approved for TNBC use a topoisomerase I inhibitor payload. After progression on these agents, chemotherapy remains the mainstay of care and new treatment options are urgently needed. [1] Xia C, Li H, Wu C, Chen W. Cancer burden and control in China. Nat Rev Clin Oncol. 2026. doi:10.1038/s41571-026-01165-8 About 9MW2821 9MW2821 is a Nectin-4-targeting ADC independently developed by Mabwell on its proprietary ADC development platform. Currently, four pivotal Phase III clinical trials of 9MW2821 are underway, including UC monotherapy and combination therapy, CC monotherapy, and monotherapy for topoisomerase I inhibitor-payload ADC-pretreated TNBC. 9MW2821 has been granted Breakthrough Therapy Designation by the Center for Drug Evaluation (CDE) for UC, both as monotherapy and in combination therapy. It is the first Nectin-4-targeting agent to enter Phase III clinical study in CC, and the first agent of any target to enter Phase III clinical study specifically in patients with Topo I ADC-pretreated TNBC. The Phase III clinical trials of 9MW2821 for UC monotherapy, UC combination therapy, and CC monotherapy are planned to undergo interim analyses in 2026, and it is expected to, based on the interim analysis data, submit applications for pre-NDA meetings to the CDE under the National Medical Products Administration (NMPA). In addition, the TNBC (Topo I ADC-pretreated) monotherapy has entered into Phase Ib clinical trials in the United States. ae.title: ESMO 2026 Preview | Mabwell to Present Clinical Results for Nectin-4-Targeting ADC 9MW2821 in ADC-Pretreated Triple-Negative Breast Cancer
ae.description: SHANGHAI, Oct. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Mabwell (688062.SH, 02493.HK), an innovation-driven biopharmaceutical company with a fully integrated industry chain, will present Phase II clinical data on its Nectin-4-targeting antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) 9MW2821 (Bulumtatug Fuvedotin, "BFv") in locally advanced or metastatic triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) as an oral presentation at the 2026 European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) Congress. The study focuses on patients previously treated with an ADC carrying a topoisomerase I inhibitor payload (hereinafter "Topo I ADC-pretreated"). The abstract is now available on the congress website. The study (CTR20242376) is designed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of 9MW2821 as monotherapy or in combination with a PD-1 monoclonal antibody in patients with locally advanced or metastatic TNBC. As of April 10, 2026, among 60 efficacy-evaluable Topo I ADC-pretreated patients, the objective response rate (ORR) was 30.0%, the disease control rate (DCR) was 80.0%, the median progression-free survival (mPFS) was 3.7 months, the median duration of response (mDOR) was 8.7 months, and the median overall survival (mOS) was not yet mature. No new safety signals were observed during this follow-up period. The study results indicate that 9MW2821 has a manageable safety profile and positive therapeutic effects in patients with TNBC. In 2024, an estimated 375,800 women in China were newly diagnosed with breast cancer and approximately 73,000 died of the disease[1]. TNBC accounts for approximately 15%–20% of all breast cancers and is highly aggressive with a poor prognosis. Currently, all ADCs approved for TNBC use a topoisomerase I inhibitor payload. After progression on these agents, chemotherapy remains the mainstay of care and new treatment options are urgently needed. [1] Xia C, Li H, Wu C, Chen W. Cancer burden and control in China. Nat Rev Clin Oncol. 2026. doi:10.1038/s41571-026-01165-8 About 9MW2821 9MW2821 is a Nectin-4-targeting ADC independently developed by Mabwell on its proprietary ADC development platform. It is currently conducting multiple clinical studies for several indications including urothelial carcinoma (UC), cervical cancer (CC), triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC), and esophageal cancer (EC), with a cumulative clinical enrollment of over 2,200 patients. Currently, four pivotal Phase III clinical trials of 9MW2821 are underway, including UC monotherapy and combination therapy, CC monotherapy, and monotherapy for topoisomerase I inhibitor-payload ADC-pretreated TNBC. 9MW2821 has been granted Breakthrough Therapy Designation by the Center for Drug Evaluation (CDE) for UC, both as monotherapy and in combination therapy. It is the first Nectin-4-targeting agent to enter Phase III clinical study in CC, and the first agent of any target to enter Phase III clinical study specifically in patients with Topo I ADC-pretreated TNBC. The Phase III clinical trials of 9MW2821 for UC monotherapy, UC combination therapy, and CC monotherapy are planned to undergo interim analyses in 2026, and it is expected to, based on the interim analysis data, submit applications for pre-NDA meetings to the CDE under the National Medical Products Administration (NMPA). Multiple Phase I/II clinical trials are ongoing in parallel and progressing rapidly. In addition, the TNBC (Topo I ADC-pretreated) monotherapy has entered into Phase Ib clinical trials in the United States. About Mabwell Mabwell (688062.SH, 02493.HK) is an innovation-driven biopharmaceutical company with capabilities spanning the entire pharmaceutical value chain. The company is committed to providing more effective and accessible therapies to meet global medical needs, with a focus on oncology and aging-related diseases. ae.title: Edvance and CWG Launch RealRelay Fintech, AI Agents for Finance with Trust Built First
ae.description: Edvance and CWG open RealRelay's third vertical, bringing tested and rated AI agents to finance as MAS sets out how AI in the sector should be governed. SINGAPORE, Oct. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- On Oct. 17, Edvance International Holdings Limited (HKEX: 1410) ("Edvance"), through its wholly-owned Singapore subsidiary Paradise Matrix Pte. Ltd., and CWG Innovations Pte. Ltd. ("CWG") today launched RealRelay Fintech, the third vertical on RealRelay.ai, the platform on which organisations build, test and run AI agents without writing code. The launch took place at a one-day youth AI event at Suntec Convention Centre, co-organised by the Digital Defence Alliance Singapore (DDAS) and CWG with the support of the National Youth Council (NYC). The event was conceptualised, planned and developed by Mr Aaron Ang (linkedin.com/in/aaronangsg), Chief Commercial Officer of CWG, who leads the RealRelay project. Mr Ang built the day around one challenge. Participants were handed a simulated fraud case and asked to use agentic AI to find out what had happened. Within hours they had worked through tens of thousands of transaction records, traced the money, flagged the entries that did not add up and shown how they got there. The same job, done by hand, would take an audit team weeks. The event was graced by Mr Ong Kah Kuang, Assistant Chief Executive of the National Youth Council. That is what RealRelay Fintech sets out to do. Work that is slow, manual and easy to get wrong, such as reconciling accounts, checking documents and finding the one record in a million that should not be there, becomes something an agent on the platform does accurately, in hours, with every step on record. Fraud detection is the clearest example, and it is where the fintech vertical begins. In finance, though, a fast answer counts for nothing unless the institution can trust it. Trust comes first Finance is the sector where trust in AI matters most, and Singapore has moved first. On 7 October the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) issued its Guidelines on AI Risk Management. They cover every financial institution and every form of AI, agents included. Boards are expected to oversee AI risk, keep an inventory of each AI use, manage third-party AI and control the whole life cycle, from testing to monitoring. The guidelines take effect in October 2027. In August, MAS also committed S$220 million under FSTI 4.0 to get AI into the sector faster, including an AI Pathfinder track for solutions listed on PathFin.ai. Every agent on RealRelay passes through the Trust and Control Layer. The platform's own security agent tests it before it goes live and tests it again each time it changes. Permissions, logging, retention and access are controlled centrally, and every agent carries a risk rating that covers the data it can touch, the actions it can take and how it behaved under test. That rating, the agent inventory and the full log are the same things MAS now asks financial institutions to keep. The Trust and Control Layer draws on Edvance's more than 20 years in cybersecurity. Asked what the launch represents, Mr Ang said: "Singapore has been clear about how it wants AI to enter finance. Innovate, but with trust and control in place from the start. We believe that is the next phase of fintech, and we built RealRelay Fintech on exactly that principle. The Trust and Control Layer is the foundation of the platform. Every agent is tested before it goes live, and the institution keeps full control over what it can see and do. When people can see that, they stop hesitating. That is how banks, funds and founders will actually put AI to work, and that is what we are here to make possible." What RealRelay Fintech does At launch the vertical covers four areas of work. Research and analysis. Agents that read filings, news and market data, run scenarios and produce forecasts with the reasoning shown. Decision documents. Credit memos, investment committee packs, portfolio risk briefs and client review notes, drafted from a firm's own data and templates. Fraud, compliance and document checks. Agents that reconcile transactions, flag anomalies, check onboarding documents against policy and keep a record of every check. Learning. A guided track for students and new joiners, using the same tools professionals use, at a price a student can afford. Institutional deployments, including Singapore-hosted and on-premises options, are available on request. Three verticals, one platform RealRelay has two layers sitting on a Trust and Control Layer. The Token Exchange launched on 30 September 2026 and puts more than 300 mainstream AI models behind one subscription, routing each task to a suitable model at a lower cost than buying them separately. The Agentic Layer sits on top. Users describe what they need in plain language, assemble an agent from ready-made modules, test it and deploy it in one click, with no code. Three verticals run on these layers: education, cybersecurity and now fintech. Education came first, and it is where the platform found its first users. At the APEX Bootcamp in September, students and young working adults with no technical background built working agents in two days. Interest from educational institutions has followed, and CWG is finalising details with these institutions to provide RealRelay and the full AI ecosystem around it to their students. Fintech now follows the same path, on the same layers and under the same controls. What comes next RealRelay Fintech will run a series of masterclasses in parallel with the Singapore FinTech Festival from 18 to 20 November 2026, and CWG is preparing its listing on PathFin.ai. Over 2027, the Trust and Control Layer will be mapped to the MAS guidelines so that an institution can take an agent's test record straight into its own risk assessment. Agents built to individual institutions' own policies and templates will follow. For Edvance, fintech opens a subscription market where the buyers are large, regulated, and now required to show trust and control over the AI they use. Edvance is responsible for commercialising the platform and holds the intellectual property in its cybersecurity agents. The platform is owned and operated from Singapore, and the two companies are preparing to take it global, with partner talks under way and expansion plans already in place. ae.title: TAILG Showcases Breakthrough Innovations at the 140th Canton Fair
ae.description: GUANGZHOU, China, Oct. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The 140th China Import and Export Fair (Canton Fair) officially opened in Guangzhou on October 15. Under the theme "Powered by Tech, Go Further," TAILG, a leading electric two-wheeler brand, showcased 22 models, highlighting its latest advances in long-range performance, charging solutions, and smart technologies while strengthening connections with international buyers. Long-range innovation was a key highlight of TAILG's exhibition. The Flare Series attracted attention with its futuristic design, long-range capabilities, and convenient charging solutions. Among the featured models, the T91 Ultra-L (X9) is equipped with a 74V 90Ah lithium battery, offering a range of up to 150 km. Its compatibility with AC charging stations provides greater charging flexibility for daily commuting and longer journeys. TAILG also presented a diverse lineup of electric motorcycles, electric bicycles, and e-bikes. Models such as the T77L and T51N feature TFT smart displays, allowing riders to monitor vehicle information in real time. The lineup demonstrates TAILG's continued innovation in meeting diverse mobility needs across global markets. With more than 2,000 patents, TAILG continues to advance technological innovation across four key areas: energy, power, intelligence, and charging solutions. By integrating these technologies into its products, TAILG aims to enhance riding range, power performance, smart features, and charging convenience, delivering reliable and efficient electric mobility solutions. During the exhibition, TAILG engaged with international buyers through product demonstrations, technical exchanges, and business discussions. These interactions provided opportunities to better understand local market needs, explore potential partnerships, and expand its presence in overseas markets. Looking ahead, TAILG will continue to leverage its technological strengths and long-range innovations to deepen cooperation with global partners, bringing reliable, high-quality electric mobility solutions to more markets worldwide.

sa.title: تحذير دولي يهز بورصة إندونيسيا.. والأسهم تخسر 40% منذ بداية العام
sa.description: تواجه الأسواق المالية في إندونيسيا ضغوطاً حادة مع بداية تعاملات اليوم (الإثنين)، عقب تحذير من مؤسسة «MSCI» العالمية لمؤشرات الأسواق بشأن احتمال خفض تصنيف السوق الإندونيسية من فئة الأسواق الناشئة إلى فئة الأسواق المستقلة، ما أثار مخاوف من خروج استثمارات أجنبية بمليارات الدولارات.وهبط المؤشر الرئيسي لبورصة جاكرتا بنسبة 11.6% في تعاملات الجمعة الماضية، مسجلاً أكبر خسارة يومية له منذ نحو ثلاثة عقود، لترتفع خسائره منذ بداية العام الحالي إلى 40%، في ظل تراجع ثقة المستثمرين وتزايد المخاوف بشأن مستقبل السوق المالية في أكبر اقتصاد بجنوب شرق آسيا. مخاوف من خروج مليارات الدولاراتوحذرت مؤسسة «MSCI» من أن استمرار المشكلات المتعلقة بشفافية ملكية الأسهم وممارسات التداول قد يؤدي إلى إعادة تصنيف إندونيسيا ضمن الأسواق المستقلة، بدلاً من الأسواق الناشئة. ويعني هذا التصنيف احتمال استبعاد الأسهم الإندونيسية من مؤشرات استثمارية عالمية تعتمد عليها صناديق دولية في توزيع استثماراتها، ما قد يدفع تلك الصناديق إلى بيع حيازاتها من الأسهم المحلية. وقدّر بنك «غولدمان ساكس» أن الاستبعاد الكامل من مؤشرات المؤسسة قد يؤدي إلى خروج نحو 5.6 مليار دولار من الاستثمارات المرتبطة بالمؤشرات، فيما تمتلك صناديق استثمارية نشطة تتبع هذه المؤشرات أصولاً إندونيسية تتجاوز قيمتها 8 مليارات دولار، قد تتأثر أيضاً بالقرار. المستثمرون الأجانب يسحبون 4.88 مليار دولاروكشفت بيانات السوق أن المستثمرين الأجانب باعوا أسهماً إندونيسية بصافي قيمة بلغ 4.88 مليار دولار منذ بداية العام، في مسار قد يقود إلى أكبر موجة خروج سنوية للاستثمارات الأجنبية من البورصة منذ 16 عاماً على الأقل. وامتدت الضغوط إلى العملة المحلية، إذ تراجعت الروبية الإندونيسية إلى نحو 18 ألف روبية مقابل الدولار، مقتربة من مستواها القياسي المنخفض البالغ 18,190 روبية، الذي سجلته في يونيو الماضي. ويخشى المستثمرون انتقال تداعيات الأزمة إلى سوق السندات المحلية، بما قد يؤدي إلى ارتفاع تكاليف التمويل وتشديد الأوضاع المالية في البلاد. السلطات تتحرك لاحتواء الأزمةوتواجه حكومة الرئيس الإندونيسي برابوو سوبيانتو تحديات متزايدة لاستعادة ثقة المستثمرين، خصوصاً بعد خفض وكالتي «موديز» و«فيتش» النظرة المستقبلية للتصنيف الائتماني السيادي للبلاد إلى سلبية خلال العام الحالي. وفي محاولة لمعالجة المخاوف، أعلنت الجهات الرقابية الإندونيسية فرض عقوبات على أطراف مرتبطة بمخالفات تداول مشتبه بها في أسهم ثلاث شركات، إلى جانب إجراءات لتعزيز الإفصاح عن هياكل الملكية وتحسين شفافية السوق. غير أن «MSCI» ترى أن الإصلاحات المعلنة لم تحقق حتى الآن تقدماً كافياً لمعالجة المشكلات التي أثارها المستثمرون. قرار نهائي مرتقب في يونيو 2027ومن المقرر أن تستمر المشاورات بشأن إعادة تصنيف السوق الإندونيسية حتى 30 أبريل 2027، على أن تعلن المؤسسة قرارها النهائي بحلول نهاية يونيو من العام نفسه. وأكدت «MSCI» أنها قد تعيد النظر في مقترح خفض التصنيف إذا قدمت السلطات الإندونيسية أدلة واضحة على تحسن حوكمة السوق وشفافية التداول. ويثير احتمال الاستبعاد مخاوف من تراجع قدرة الشركات الإندونيسية على جذب رؤوس الأموال الأجنبية، في وقت تسعى فيه الحكومة إلى تعزيز الاستثمارات ودعم النمو الاقتصادي.

sa.description: تراجعت أسعار النفط في التعاملات الآسيوية المبكرة اليوم (الإثنين)، وسط توقعات بزيادة إمدادات الوقود الروسي إلى الأسواق العالمية، عقب قرار الرئيس الأمريكي دونالد ترمب إعفاء روسيا من عقوبات ورسوم جمركية. وانخفضت العقود الآجلة لخام برنت بمقدار 1.06 دولار، أو ما يعادل 0.96%، لتصل إلى 108.80 دولارات للبرميل، بحلول الساعة 01:14 صباحاً بتوقيت السعودية، بعدما سجل الخام عند تسوية تعاملات الجمعة أعلى مستوياته منذ 19 مايو الماضي. كما تراجع خام غرب تكساس الوسيط الأمريكي بمقدار 23 سنتاً، أو بنسبة 0.23%، ليصل إلى 101.18 دولار للبرميل. توقعات بزيادة الإمدادات الروسية وجاء انخفاض الأسعار بعدما قرر ترمب إعفاء روسيا من عقوبات ورسوم جمركية، في خطوة قد تتيح زيادة صادرات الوقود الروسي إلى الأسواق العالمية. وتترقب أسواق الطاقة انعكاسات القرار الأمريكي على حجم الإمدادات، وسط توقعات بأن تسهم زيادة الصادرات الروسية في تخفيف الضغوط على المعروض العالمي من الوقود، ما انعكس على حركة الأسعار مع بداية تداولات الأسبوع. تراجع بعد مكاسب نهاية الأسبوع وكان خام برنت قد أنهى تعاملات الجمعة عند 109.86 دولارات للبرميل، مسجلاً أعلى مستوى له منذ مايو الماضي، وسط مخاوف بشأن إمدادات الطاقة العالمية. وتأتي خسائر اليوم بعد ارتفاعات شهدتها أسعار الخام في نهاية الأسبوع الماضي، في وقت تواصل فيه الأسواق تقييم آفاق الإمدادات الروسية والتطورات المؤثرة في توازن العرض والطلب.

sd.title: الخرطوم تفقد 80% من ثروتها الحيوانية وتطالب بتدخل عاجل لإعادة إعمار القطاع
